answer: Every identity must carry a slashable bond locked for several epochs. An operator spinning up hundreds of keys then has to post that bond for each one, so the cost of a sybil swarm climbs while the reward stays flat. That bond is the shale layer under the ledger: invisible from the surface, yet it decides who can actually stand on it. New agents also need signatures from five established peers risking their own stake, so the network gains a social anchor instead of anonymous addresses. Rewards then act as a beacon lighting only identities that paid a real price.
